title: Deterministic prefill serializer + replay smoke harness for CUDA Graph stability
creator: Priya Raman
description: Problem: Non-deterministic state during prefill/capture and subtle divergence on multi-stream replay intermittently causes token-level mismatches or kernel hangups in long-running hosts. Goal: Implement a lightweight deterministic prefill serializer to canonicalize temporary KV/prefill state and add a replay smoke harness that can run at scale in CI and on-dedicated pools to catch regressions early. This ticket covers design, a minimal on-device serializer, an off-device replay validator, and CI integration for nightly fuzz/replay runs.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic serializer produces stable, byte-comparable prefill artifacts for a representative set of workloads (chat + code + short prompt).
A replay smoke harness can replay captured artifacts against the current runtime and report token divergence and kernel errors with stack traces.
CI job added that runs the smoke harness on a small fleet of representative traces nightly and fails on any divergence above threshold (>0.1% token mismatch for large-batch traces).
End-to-end latency overhead of serialization + small validation replay is <= 3% in dedicated pre-release runs (measured on p4d-like machines).
Design doc and implementation PRs reviewed by runtime and reliability leads and merged behind a feature flag.
implementation_notes: Serializer will be intentionally minimal: capture KV keys, epoch counters, seq lengths, and prefill token hashes rather than full embeddings to keep artifacts small.
Store artifacts as compressed, signed protobuf blobs to preserve compatibility across runtime revisions; signing allows detection of accidental mutation in storage. Use LZ4 compression for speed.

Replay harness will run a staged validation: (1) dry-run decode using captured kernel selection hints, (2) full decode with current kernel selection, (3) token-by-token comparison with configurable tolerance.
test_plan: Unit tests for serializer round-trip determinism with seeded workloads.
Integration test that captures a prefill on an older runtime, replays on HEAD and fails if divergence exceeds threshold.
Add synthetic jittered multi-stream traces to CI to exercise prefill concurrency paths.
Run smoke harness on Dedicated pool nightly; aggregate failures into an oncall alert with link to artifact for debugging.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Priya Raman: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed to prioritize smallest possible on-device format; avoid embedding dumps to reduce size. Agreed feature-flag gated rollout.

2025-02-18 - Alex Moreno: Spike complete. Serializer prototype produces 3-5x smaller artifacts than full-state dump for sample chat traces. Observed deterministic ordering issues due to unordered hash map in KV snapshot—will canonicalize by key sort.
2025-02-24 - Mei Chen (Reliability): Reviewed proto layout. Requested inclusion of runtime-version metadata and kernel-selection hints for better triage when replays diverge.
2025-03-03 - Alex Moreno: Implemented LZ4 + protobuf encoding. Added signature header. Initial replay harness can detect two classes of failure: token mismatch and kernel error (cudaLaunch failure).

2025-03-06 - Code review feedback: Split serializer into interface + backend to allow future on-disk binary formats; reduce public surface of runtime headers. Request to add a flaky-test tolerant threshold in CI to avoid noisy alerts from benign hardware jitter.
2025-03-10 - Performance check: Serialization adds 1.8% wall time for representative prefill workloads on p4d. Replay validation (in isolated run) adds 2.5% overall. Both within target.
2025-03-12 - Priya Raman: Moving to In Progress. Next: finish PR reviews, add nightly CI integration, and prepare runbook for investigating replay artifacts.
